frozenSources.role: the JSON reader the rule path reaches: getString is the field-text boundary this corpus compares
the rule splitter and {$.rule} inner-rule pass AnalyzeByJSonPath.getString runs before the read

library.wraps: gradle/libs.versions.toml:22, the version the frozen AnalyzeByJSonPath.kt calls

note: Frozen inputs for the JSONPath reader. Every document here is the exact text JsonPath.parse receives, and every rule is passed to AnalyzeByJSonPath.getString, so the golden is the frozen field text. A case with a `declared` block is one the capability matrix already names; the comparator reports it in its notCompared list with the frozen text it could not match and refuses a declared row that turns out to compare. Notes name the frozen form a row reaches, not the answer: the golden holds the answer.

cases.name: filter-eq-number-matches-string-one
cases.note: The filter form the used sources reach. The ValueNodes comparison keeps the row whose value is the *string* "1" as well, so three rows match and getString joins them with a newline.

cases.name: filter-eq-spaced
cases.note: The same comparison with the spaces FilterCompiler allows around the operator.

cases.name: filter-eq-single-quotes
cases.note: A single-quoted string operand.

cases.name: filter-eq-double-quotes
cases.note: A double-quoted string operand; the compiler's QUOTE token accepts both.

cases.name: filter-gt-number
cases.note: A numeric comparison over a field one row lacks and one row holds as null.

cases.name: filter-lt-number
cases.note: The other side of the same comparison.

cases.name: filter-gt-string-field
cases.note: A numeric literal against a field that is a string: ValueNodes parses the *operand* and compares strings by their parsed value.

cases.name: filter-ge-string-operand
cases.note: A quoted operand against the same string field.

cases.name: filter-le-number
cases.note: The inclusive comparison, with a row whose field is null.

cases.name: filter-ne-number
cases.note: The inequality, which the missing-field row also satisfies.

cases.name: filter-regex-anchored
cases.note: =~ is Matcher.matches, so the pattern is anchored over the whole value.

cases.name: filter-regex-ignore-case
cases.note: The i flag is one of the two the adapter runs.

cases.name: filter-regex-ungrouped-alternation
cases.note: Matcher.matches over an alternation: /a|ab/ matches 'a' and 'ab' but not 'ab' by the first branch, so the anchoring decides this row.

cases.name: filter-regex-end-anchor
cases.note: A $ anchor, and a row whose value is missing entirely.

cases.name: filter-regex-empty-value
cases.note: An empty pattern matches the empty string, not the missing value.

cases.name: filter-regex-on-array-element
cases.note: A filter applied to the elements of a nested array, where the operand is the element itself.

cases.name: filter-in-numbers
cases.note: The in operator, which the adapter's operator set names.

cases.name: filter-nin-numbers
cases.note: Its negation.

cases.name: filter-in-strings
cases.note: An in operand of strings against the same mixed field.

cases.name: filter-size-title
cases.note: The size operator over a string field.

cases.name: filter-size-tags
cases.note: The same operator over an array field.

cases.name: filter-empty-empty-string-true
cases.note: empty true over a field that is an empty string in one row and absent in another.

cases.name: filter-empty-empty-string-false
cases.note: The other polarity.

cases.name: filter-empty-tags-true
cases.note: empty over an array field, where one row's array is empty.

cases.name: filter-exists-true
cases.note: exists true, measured against a field one row lacks and one row holds as a value.

cases.name: filter-exists-null-value
cases.note: exists over a key whose value is null: the corner that decides whether a present null counts as present.

cases.name: filter-truthiness-null-value
cases.note: The bare existence form the compiler rewrites to exists true.

cases.name: filter-eq-null
cases.note: == null against the literal, over rows that have the key and rows that do not.

cases.name: filter-ne-null
cases.note: Its negation, which the missing-key rows satisfy.

cases.name: filter-empty-null-true
cases.note: empty true over a null value.

cases.name: filter-bare-boolean-field
cases.note: A bare boolean field, which the compiler rewrites to == true rather than to an existence check.

cases.name: filter-bare-boolean-eq-true
cases.note: The explicit spelling of the same comparison.

cases.name: filter-tags-eq-list
cases.note: A list literal as an == operand, which RelationalOperator compares with ValueNodes by list value.

cases.name: filter-and
cases.note: A filter whose rule-level && also appears inside the filter: the splitter must not cut this rule, and the filter's own && is the library's.

cases.name: filter-or
cases.note: The same for ||.

cases.name: filter-not
cases.note: A negated group.

cases.name: filter-missing-field
cases.note: A field no row has: the filter matches nothing and the reader leaves the empty text.

cases.name: filter-missing-field-eq
cases.note: A comparison against a field no row has.

cases.name: filter-scalar-array
cases.note: A filter over an array of scalars, where the operand is the element itself.

cases.name: filter-scalar-array-eq
cases.note: A string comparison over scalar elements.

cases.name: slice-between
cases.note: ArraySliceOperation's between form over the matched rows' content.

cases.name: slice-from-start
cases.note: Its from-start form.

cases.name: slice-to-end
cases.note: Its to-end form.

cases.name: slice-negative-from-end
cases.note: A negative start, which resolves from the array's end.

cases.name: slice-negative-to-end
cases.note: A negative end, which resolves from the array's end.

cases.name: slice-negative-both
cases.note: A negative end in the between form: SLICE_BETWEEN does not resolve it, which the matrix row records.

cases.name: slice-third-field-ignored
cases.note: ArraySliceOperation.parse reads three fields and the third is not a step: the matrix row records that [a:b:c] behaves as [a:b].

cases.name: slice-past-end
cases.note: A window past the end of the array.

cases.name: slice-reversed
cases.note: A start beyond the end: the slice keeps the array's order and this one is empty.

cases.name: slice-then-index
cases.note: An index applied to a slice's result.

cases.name: slice-then-key-index
cases.note: A nested key and index under a slice, where one of the two rows has no tags.

cases.name: slice-of-strings
cases.note: A slice over an array of strings; getString joins the definite array's elements.

cases.name: index-negative
cases.note: A negative index, which resolves from the array's end.

cases.name: index-multi
cases.note: The index-list form, which the matrix row names.

cases.name: index-wildcard
cases.note: The wildcard index over the rows.

cases.name: index-ascii
cases.note: A plain positive index.

cases.name: plain-slice
cases.note: A negative index over the string array.

cases.name: scan-recursive-title
cases.note: A recursive scan collecting every title, including the empty string one row holds.

cases.name: dot-leading-filter-is-recursive
cases.note: PathCompiler prefixes a dot-leading path with $., so this is the recursive scan, and the matched value is an object: the field text renders it through toString.

cases.name: index-out-of-range-negative
cases.note: An index past the array's start.

cases.name: render-empty-object
cases.note: A whole empty object, which is the one shape an empty container needs its own form for.

cases.name: render-empty-array
cases.note: A whole empty array.

cases.name: render-array-of-mixed-scalars
cases.note: One array with an int, a double, a boolean, null, a string with a comma, an empty object and an empty array, so one row pins the item separator, the quoting rule and the empty-container forms inside a list.

cases.name: render-nested-containers
cases.note: An array of an array and of an object, so the nested forms are rendered by the container rules rather than by the flat ones.

cases.name: render-quoted-strings
cases.note: Strings carrying a double quote, a backslash, a tab and non-ASCII characters, joined as the elements of a definite array: the frozen reader does not quote or escape here, it takes the element texts apart the same way it takes a scalar. The nested case is render-nested-quoted-strings.

cases.name: render-numbers-map
cases.note: A map of an int at Integer.MAX_VALUE, an integral double, a negative double and an integer past 2^53: the number forms the two runtimes must agree on.

cases.name: render-map-with-container-values
cases.note: A map whose values are a string with a comma, an array, a nested map with a null, a boolean and a non-ASCII string.

cases.name: render-objects-in-array
cases.note: Objects as array elements, where the object form is chosen by the array renderer rather than by the join.

cases.name: render-slice-of-objects
cases.note: The slice form with no scalar leaf, so the joined values are the matched rows themselves.

cases.name: render-filter-of-object
cases.note: A recursive filter whose match is an object, so the join carries one rendered map.

cases.name: render-index-of-object
cases.note: A definite index naming one object: the frozen reader takes the toString of the single value rather than joining a list.

cases.name: render-array-of-arrays
cases.note: An indefinite path whose matches are arrays, so each match is rendered by the array rule and then joined.

cases.name: render-nested-quoted-strings
cases.note: A map holding the quoted strings, a number list with a double, a boolean and a null, and the two empty containers, so one row pins what the array form does to each of them while nested. The strings carry a quote, a backslash, a tab, a newline and non-ASCII characters.

cases.name: declared-scan-index-guard
cases.note: A row the capability matrix already names, kept in the corpus so the comparator reports it rather than skipping it.

declared.reason: The matrix row names `$..[N]...` as refused by name: the frozen ScanPathToken.walkArray element-index guard is what decides what it answers, and this reader refuses the form instead of guessing it. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

cases.name: declared-scan-wildcard
cases.note: A row the capability matrix already names, kept in the corpus so the comparator reports it rather than skipping it.

declared.reason: The same guard reached through the `$..*.` spelling. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

cases.name: declared-operator-triple-equals
cases.note: A row the capability matrix already names, kept in the corpus so the comparator reports it rather than skipping it.

declared.reason: The library knows `===` and this reader does not run it, which the matrix row names. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

cases.name: declared-operator-contains
cases.note: A row the capability matrix already names, kept in the corpus so the comparator reports it rather than skipping it.

declared.reason: `contains` is one of the operators the matrix row lists as not run. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

cases.name: declared-operator-subsetof
cases.note: A row the capability matrix already names, kept in the corpus so the comparator reports it rather than skipping it.

cases.name: declared-function-in-filter-path
cases.note: A row the capability matrix already names, kept in the corpus so the comparator reports it rather than skipping it.

declared.reason: A function call in a filter path, which the matrix row lists among the refused path forms. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

cases.name: declared-quoted-property
cases.note: A row the capability matrix already names, kept in the corpus so the comparator reports it rather than skipping it.

declared.reason: A quoted property name, refused by name in the matrix row. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

cases.name: declared-slice-step
cases.note: A row the capability matrix already names, kept in the corpus so the comparator reports it rather than skipping it.

declared.reason: `[::n]` is refused by the library and by this reader, so the compared text the frozen side would carry is the empty one getString leaves — the two shapes differ and the matrix row names both. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

cases.name: declared-slice-all
cases.note: A row the capability matrix already names, kept in the corpus so the comparator reports it rather than skipping it.

cases.name: declared-slice-over-map
cases.note: A row the capability matrix already names, kept in the corpus so the comparator reports it rather than skipping it.

declared.reason: The recorded divergence in the matrix row: a definite slice over a non-array is a named FormatException where the frozen reader swallows the library PathNotFoundException into an empty text. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

cases.name: declared-slice-over-null
cases.note: A row the capability matrix already names, kept in the corpus so the comparator reports it rather than skipping it.

declared.reason: The same divergence over a null value. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]
